description: Solo team from New Delhi, building a story driven web experience about NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars. Combining pixel art, writing and web development into an interactive tour of the sites and hardware left behind.
summary: Last Signal is an interactive scroll-driven storybook for ages 10–14 about five historic machines NASA left across the solar system: the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Spirit, Ingenuity, and Voyager 1. As users scroll, each chapter presents a custom 3D model, spoken and typed first-person narration, verified mission facts, and a unique "last signal" sound synthesized from real mission data. When scrolling past the chapter, each machine fades into the state of its actual mission end, and scrolling back up repairs it.
details:
• What it does: An immersive, scroll-driven educational web story for children (ages 10-14) that brings abandoned space exploration history to life through interactive 3D models, narration, and audio telemetry.
  • How it works: Built using a single-file index.html structure paired with Three.js for real-time 3D rendering and Web Audio API for browser-synthesized sounds. As users scroll through the chapters, camera angles shift, models dynamically transition into their historical "signal lost" or "left behind" breakdown states, and browser text-to-speech narrates each spacecraft's first-person story.
  • What we hope to achieve: To make forgotten space missions memorable and engaging for kids, turning historical telemetry and engineering milestones into an emotional, interactive storytelling experience.
  • Tools & Languages used: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js (3D WebGL engine), Web Audio API, browser Text-to-Speech synthesis, Python (trimesh) for generating 3D models. Hosted and deployed via Vercel.
